title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 137-139). Grothendieck is axiomatising 'ateliers'. These appear to be his 1986 framework for a 'tame' geometry of figures, the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse. Here A is an atelier and F is a figure, i.e. a finite partition into A-pieces, with poset of strata F~. G ≪ F means G refines F: there is an increasing map φ: G~ → F~ with each stratum Y of G 'interior-contained' in the stratum φ(Y) of F.

Page 137 proposes, as the definition of 'G is a subdivision of F', condition (i): for every X in F~, the fibre φ^{-1}(X) fills X, i.e. supp° φ^{-1}(X) = X°. Assuming an axiom he calls 'Atmag supp', (i) is said to be equivalent to:
- (ii) supp G = supp F;
- (iii) there is no A-object Z with Z ≪ F that is interior-disjoint from G.

This page adds the following.
- (iv), when A is 'divisible': (iii) can be checked on the lattice L of the atelier. There is no x ∈ L that is open in F (x ∈ Ouv(F), i.e. x ≪ F) and disjoint from G (x |0| G).
- Proof structure: (i)⇒(ii)⇒(iii)⇒(iv) are trivial. (iv)⇒(i) under divisibility reduces to (iii)⇒(i), which was obtained from the support axiom.
- (v), also equivalent under divisibility: G is maximal among refinements of F ordered by inclusion. A subdivision is thus a refinement that cannot be enlarged, i.e. one that leaves no 'hole'. When these hold he calls G a subdivision of F.

He then drafts and strikes out a stronger candidate condition. It says the Alexandrov (order) topology of F~ is the quotient of that of G~ under φ. Equivalently, X ≤ X' in F~ iff there exist Y ∈ φ^{-1}(X) and Y' ∈ φ^{-1}(X') with Y ≤ Y'. This is the combinatorial statement that the face order of the coarse stratification is generated by that of the subdivision. He begins to interpret it for a concrete atelier ('A = Fig(...)', likely Euclidean or PL figures). The next page continues: F is obtained from G by 'regrouping' strata, with the order on F's index set deduced by regrouping. That is also crossed out.

Two marginal notes express doubt about the conditions or the order of exposition ('est-il judicieux ... Voire!').

The problem served is a purely order- and lattice-theoretic definition of subdivision for stratified tame figures. Such a definition would let one later compare a figure with its subdivisions (invariance, cofinality of subdivisions), as for PL or o-minimal cell decompositions.
errors: The chain of equivalences depends on undefined, unverified axioms ('Atmag supp', 'divisibilité'). On the page, (iv)⇒(i) and (v)⇔(i) are asserted, not proved.

The quotient-topology condition is not implied by (i)-(v) in general. A refinement filling the support need not reflect the face order unless frontier conditions hold. This is presumably why it is struck out and why the margin expresses doubt.
The notation (≪, interior-containment, |0|, Ouv(F)) is used loosely. 'Z ∈ L' on the first line and 'x ∈ L' in (iv) suggest a shift between atelier objects and lattice elements.

ideas.what: Subdivision of a stratified figure defined as a refinement with the same support / no uncovered open piece / maximal refinement
ideas.modern_name: subdivision of a cell or stratified complex; refinement of o-minimal cell decompositions / stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman); in tame/o-minimal setting van den Dries and others (1980s-90s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'topologie modérée' is in the Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the atelier formalism is unpublished.

ideas.what: Lattice-theoretic formulation (iv) via open elements of a lattice disjoint from G, under a 'divisibility' axiom
ideas.modern_name: point-free / lattice-theoretic description of definable sets (Boolean algebra of definable sets, spectral/type-space view)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality/model theory (Pillay-Steinhorn, Knight); locales and point-free topology

ideas.what: Struck condition: the Alexandrov topology of the coarse stratum poset is the quotient of that of the subdivision's poset under the carrier map
ideas.modern_name: carrier map of a subdivision as a quotient of face posets / exit-path or stratified poset maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: combinatorial topology of face posets (Björner and others); stratified spaces over posets (Lurie, Higher Algebra, Appendix A)

missed.claim: Grothendieck attempts to characterise subdivisions in an abstract axiomatic 'atelier' by several equivalent order/lattice conditions. These include maximality among refinements and a quotient-of-Alexandrov-topology condition. He abandons the latter with explicit doubt. The axiomatic framework itself (ateliers, divisibility, Atmag supp) is an unpublished attempt at foundations of tame topology, parallel to o-minimality.
missed.quote: G est maximal parmi les raffinements de F, ordonnés par ⊂ ... La top. de F~ (associée à sa structure d'ordre) est quotient de celle de G~
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Stratified spaces modelled over posets (exit-path ∞-categories, Lurie, Ayala-Francis-Tanaka) need exactly such conditions on maps of stratifying posets for refinements to be 'subdivisions'. Grothendieck's lattice-theoretic version is an early, independent, unpublished formulation. Its value is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a definitional draft of subdivision in the unpublished atelier formalism. The individual conditions are standard in spirit. What is mildly notable is the lattice/maximality formulation and the struck Alexandrov-quotient condition, an early poset-stratification viewpoint, in a framework not documented in the literature.
transcription_corrections: The words after '(iv) ⇒ (i) (moyennant divisibilité)' appear to read 'résulte de (iii) ⇒ (i), qui n'utilise que [?] Atmag supp?'. The axiom name 'Atmag supp?' is written on its own line, matching page 137, rather than 'a été supposé'.
First line: 'Quand A est divisible, [crossed] Z ∈ L, et ... prend la forme' — the condition (iii) takes the form (iv).
The insertion after 'ces conditions' reads approximately 'sont satisfaites' over the crossed word, not '[-...-] par'.
Left margin text is approximately: 'NB Ces conditions de maximalité/d'équivalence me paraissent peu ... ?' and 'est-il judicieux de l'exiger d'abord? Voire!'. The readings are uncertain.
Last line: 'dans le cas A = Fig(...)' — the second word is illegible; 'Euc' is a guess.
